member.name: T:SysWeaver.Auth.DataProtection
member.summary: Protects stored personal / secret values (e-mail addresses, phone numbers, user names, API keys ...) using a random program secret that is stored outside of the data (in , unique per application and computer). A leaked database (or data file) doesn't reveal the values without the secret, which needs access to the machine.
member.remarks:
For every protected value:
A lookup hash (): HMAC-SHA256(secret, kind + "\0" + normalized value), indexable, used to find a row from a value (ex: e-mail => user id).
A per row random value (), replaced on every change.
The encrypted value (): AES-256-GCM with the key HMAC-SHA256(secret, "enc\0" + kind + "\0" + random) and a random nonce, stored as nonce (12 bytes) + cipher text + tag (16 bytes). Used to get the value back (ex: the e-mail address of a user).
IMPORTANT: if the secret is lost (ex: the key value store folder is deleted, or the data is moved to another computer) the protected values can't be read or found. Applications (or computers) that share the same data must use the same secret (see ). Thread safe.

member.name: T:SysWeaver.Auth.SimpleAuthorizer
member.summary: A simple authorizer with a static set of users defined in the parameters and/or a (monitored) file, and optional API keys.
member.remarks: Users are defined as "user:password:tokens:domain" strings, see . The password is a SCRAM verifier ("$s1$...", see , the "Generate password hash" debug page can compute it) or clear text (validated against the password policy). Password hashes (44 char base64) are refused. API keys are only accepted as header auth (bearer / basic), never as a one time token (). API keys are stored encrypted in (see ), optionally restricted to some client addresses, and are accepted as bearer tokens (and basic auth). Header auth (basic / bearer) is only allowed for API keys, unless is true. The user guids are "SI:" followed by a hash of the user name. Thread safe, user changes are applied atomically and users whose password or tokens changed are asked to log out.
member.summary: API keys: stored encrypted in (see , the secret is stored outside of the key list). Every key has its own tokens (at least one, each "service" or "service_<scope>", see ) and an optional list of allowed client addresses / networks. An API key only gets access to what requires one of its tokens ().

Passkey storage of the simple authorizer (the passkey methods). The passkeys of all users are stored as one array in (few users, so a simple storage is fine). Enabled by , the token based methods (QR code, links, sign up) aren't supported.

Stored users: users added at run time (web API / the "Users" page), stored encrypted in like the API keys. A stored user has a SCRAM verifier ("$s1$...", made by the "Generate password hash" page or the "hash" verb of the service host) and tokens. Managed by users with the tokens ("admin" or "debug"); an "admin" without "debug" can't give the "debug" token, and can't change or remove a user that has it. The users of the configuration and the user file can't be changed here, and a stored user can't replace them.

member.name: F:SysWeaver.Auth.SimpleAuthorizerParams.Users
member.summary: One user per string with the following syntax: "username:password". Auth tokens can be specified by appending a colon (:) or bar (|) and a comma separated list of tokens, ex: "username:password:token1, token2, token3" An application specific domain can be appended after another colon or bar, ex: "username:password:tokens:domain". The password may therefore not contain ':' or '|'. Password should be a SCRAM verifier: "$s1$iterations$salt$storedKey" (see , generated using the "Generate password hash" page). A verifier can't be used to sign in, it must be brute forced (PBKDF2 per guess) to find the password. Password can also be clear text (hashed and turned into a verifier when loaded). Verifiers are unique per user per application (, default is the entry assembly name). A 44 char password that is valid base64 of 32 bytes is a password hash, not a password: such users are skipped with a warning. Clear text passwords must fulfill the , users with invalid passwords are skipped. Users with a too long name (over chars) or domain (over chars) are skipped with a warning message, the other users are still loaded. User names are case insensitive (the last definition of a name wins), white spaces around the parts are trimmed, empty lines and lines starting with "#" or "//" are ignored. The user guid is "SI:" followed by a hash of the user name (as written, case sensitive).

member.name: F:SysWeaver.Auth.SimpleAuthorizerParams.PasswordPolicy
member.summary: The requirements for clear text passwords, null uses the default policy.

member.name: F:SysWeaver.Auth.SimpleAuthorizerParams.AllowBasicAuth
member.summary: If true (and the server accepts the Authorization header), then the users of the file / configuration are also allowed to login using basic auth. By default (false) only API keys can use header auth (basic / bearer), they are meant for services (the users of the file / configuration sign in with the login page). Basic auth compares the password hash (no PBKDF2 per request), so it only works for users defined with a clear text password.

member.name: F:SysWeaver.Auth.SimpleAuthorizerParams.ApiKeyAuth
member.summary: If non-null, API keys can be created and deleted, and this is the tokens of a new key when none are given (comma separated). Every key has its own tokens: at least one, each "service" or "service_<scope>" (see ), an invalid value here disables API keys (with an error message). API keys can be used as bearer tokens, and they are allowed to use basic auth (http server still need to allow for it). An API key only gets access to what requires one of its tokens, never to what any logged in user may use (an empty requirement, see ). A "service_<scope>" token also fulfills a "service" requirement, only the "service_<scope>" token fulfills a "service_<scope>" requirement.
